exposure: COVID-19 related restrictive measures (suspension of visiting periods, mandatory mask-wearing, suspension of companionship during childbirth, cancellation of prenatal exercises, antenatal talks, hospital tours, and postnatal classes)
outcome: Methods of intrapartum pain relief (pethidine use, birthing ball use)
cohort: The study compared women who delivered in a tertiary university public hospital in Hong Kong between the pre-alert COVID-19 period (Jan 1, 2019 to Jan 4, 2020) and the post-alert COVID-19 period (Jan 5, 2020 to Apr 30, 2020).
finding: Pregnant women in the post-alert COVID-19 period reported significantly more depressive symptoms (EPDS scores >=10) 1 day after delivery (14.4% vs 11.9%; P<0.05) and there was a 13.1% reduction in the number of deliveries compared to the pre-alert period.
mod_finding: More women used pethidine (6.2% vs 4.6%) and fewer used a birthing ball (8.5% vs 12.4%) for pain relief during labour in the post-alert group.
